# Merging Positions

The Ramsey decomposition needs a second finite-index equivalence, this time on the **positions** of an $\omega$-word. Fix a congruence $\equiv$ on finite words. For positions $k,k'$ and a later position $m>\max\{k,k'\}$, say $k$ and $k'$ **merge at $m$**, written $k\mathrel{\widetilde{=}}_{\alpha,m}k'$, if the two segments reaching $m$ agree:
$$ \alpha(k,m)\ \equiv\ \alpha(k',m). $$

The stopping point $m$ is ours to choose; the same two positions may fail to merge at one $m$ and succeed at a later one. But **[persistence](#persistence)** says: once merged, always merged.

We illustrate with the smallest possible congruence — **parity of length** $\equiv_{\mathrm{par}}$ — on the word from the chapter figure, $\alpha = b\,a\,b\,c\,c\,a\,b\,c\cdots$. Since $\equiv_{\mathrm{par}}$ ignores symbols, $\alpha(k,m)$ and $\alpha(k',m)$ have lengths $m-k$ and $m-k'$; they share parity **iff $k$ and $k'$ have the same parity as natural numbers**. (With a richer congruence like $\approx_{\mathcal A}$, merging becomes a genuine, symbol-dependent event.)

```{=html}
<div class="sc-lab" id="nb22">
  <div class="input-row">
    <div class="input-group"><label>Position k</label><select id="nb22-k"></select></div>
    <div class="input-group"><label>Position k′</label><select id="nb22-kp"></select></div>
  </div>
  <div class="sc-panel">
    <div class="posline" id="nb22-line"></div>
    <div id="nb22-detail"></div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
(function(){
  const word=['b','a','b','c','c','a','b','c'];  // positions 0..7
  const N=word.length;
  const kSel=document.getElementById('nb22-k'), kpSel=document.getElementById('nb22-kp');
  for(let i=0;i<N-1;i++){ kSel.add(new Option(i,i)); kpSel.add(new Option(i,i)); }
  kSel.value=1; kpSel.value=3;

  function firstMerge(k,kp){
    // parity congruence: segment lengths (m-k),(m-kp); merge iff same parity <=> k,kp same parity
    if(k%2!==kp%2) return null;               // never merge
    return Math.max(k,kp)+1;                   // earliest valid m
  }
  function render(){
    let k=+kSel.value, kp=+kpSel.value;
    const line=document.getElementById('nb22-line'); const detail=document.getElementById('nb22-detail');
    const m=firstMerge(k,kp);
    // draw line
    line.innerHTML='';
    for(let i=0;i<N;i++){
      const cell=document.createElement('div');
      let cls='poscell'; if(i===k)cls+=' k'; if(i===kp)cls+=' kp'; if(m!==null&&i===m)cls+=' m';
      cell.className=cls;
      cell.innerHTML=`<div class="possym">${word[i]}</div><div class="posidx">${i}</div>`;
      line.appendChild(cell);
    }
    if(m===null){
      detail.innerHTML=`<div class="verdict-box verdict-fail"><strong>Positions ${k} and ${kp} never merge.</strong> They have different parity (${k} is ${k%2?'odd':'even'}, ${kp} is ${kp%2?'odd':'even'}), so for every m the two segments differ in length by |${k}−${kp}| = ${Math.abs(k-kp)}, an odd number — opposite parities, always in different ≡par-classes.</div>`;
      return;
    }
    const lk=m-k, lkp=m-kp;
    let html=`<div class="seg">α(${k},${m}) = "${word.slice(k,m).join('')}" &nbsp; length ${lk} (${lk%2?'odd':'even'})</div>`;
    html+=`<div class="seg">α(${kp},${m}) = "${word.slice(kp,m).join('')}" &nbsp; length ${lkp} (${lkp%2?'odd':'even'})</div>`;
    html+=`<div class="verdict-box verdict-pass"><strong>${k} ⋍ ${kp} at m = ${m}.</strong> Both segments have ${lk%2?'odd':'even'} length, hence the same ≡par-class.</div>`;
    // persistence table
    html+=`<h4 style="margin-top:14px;">Persistence: once merged, always merged</h4><table class="ptable"><tr><th>m′</th>`;
    const ms=[]; for(let j=0;j<6;j++) ms.push(m+j);
    ms.forEach(mm=>html+=`<th>${mm}</th>`); html+='</tr><tr><th>len α(k,m′)%2</th>';
    ms.forEach(mm=>html+=`<td>${(mm-k)%2}</td>`); html+='</tr><tr><th>len α(k′,m′)%2</th>';
    ms.forEach(mm=>html+=`<td>${(mm-kp)%2}</td>`); html+='</tr><tr><th>merge?</th>';
    ms.forEach(mm=>html+=`<td>${(mm-k)%2===(mm-kp)%2?'✓':'✗'}</td>`); html+='</tr></table>';
    html+=`<p style="font-size:0.82rem;color:var(--sc-label);margin-top:8px;">Extending both segments by the same suffix α(${m},m′) keeps their lengths’ parity equal forever — merging cannot be broken.</p>`;
    detail.innerHTML=html;
  }
  kSel.addEventListener('change',render); kpSel.addEventListener('change',render);
  render();
})();
</script>
```

The default choice $k=1$, $k'=3$ reproduces the chapter's figure: the segments $\alpha(1,4)$ and $\alpha(3,4)$ have lengths $3$ and $1$, both odd, so they merge at $m=4$. For the parity congruence every even position merges with every even position and every odd with every odd — no real "sifting" is needed. The general Ramsey argument (**[Notebook 23](23-ramsey-decomposition.qmd)**) runs the same pigeonhole on a *richer* congruence, where finding an infinite pairwise-merging set takes genuine work.
